articles.title: Built from Scratch: How a meteorologist built a better umbrella
articles.summary: Rick Reichmuth, after 19 years as a Fox meteorologist, turned his sights on creating the perfect umbrella. Now, Weatherman sells five categories of umbrellas, ponchos, hats and more.
articles.body: Rick Reichmuth didn’t set out to start a business. He just wanted a better umbrella. After 19 years as a Fox meteorologist, he knew how to predict the weather, yet he still couldn't find an umbrella that could survive it. Staring at racks of umbrellas on the streets of New York City, he was struck by a glaring gap in the market: While categories like bandages and tissues had iconic, trusted household names, buying an umbrella was a total gamble. CEO SUNDAY: ARMY VETERAN TURNED HEALTH TECH BOSS CALLS SUPPORT FOR THOSE WHO SERVED A ‘SACRED OBLIGATION’ After searching for a standout umbrella brand and coming up empty, he asked himself, "Why not create my own?" Nobody knows the elements better than a meteorologist, and with that, Weatherman was born. Stepping out into the rain Reichmuth started by taking apart hundreds of umbrellas in his New York City apartment. His goal was simple: He wanted to reverse-engineer how they worked, pinpoint why they failed and establish the blueprint for a truly great umbrella. Armed with that research, he teamed up with an industrial designer friend to build a model that was strong, durable and built to withstand the elements. CEO SUNDAY: AVELO AIRLINES CEO REVEALS THE HABIT HE CREDITS FOR HIS SUCCESS Yet, despite a lengthy career in meteorology, nothing had prepared him for the ins and outs of running a business. Reichmuth remembers looking at the very first Weatherman prototype and thinking, "Wow, I think the hard part is finally over." As it turned out, the work was just beginning. Weathering the storm Running a small business tested Reichmuth in ways forecasting never did. He said it was a journey marked by steep trials and hard-earned lessons that he still calls the hardest thing he's ever done. When Weatherman debuted in 2017, the lineup consisted of just two designs: a collapsible model and a stick umbrella. BUILT FROM SCRATCH: HOW A RENTED KITCHEN AND HAND-SQUEEZED FRUIT BECAME A VERSATILE MIXER Both have since been retired, a testament to how relentlessly the brand has refined and upgraded its engineering over the last nine years. Entering a new industry without a product development background was intimidating, and early missteps hit hard. "Early on, a failure or setback could really knock me down," Reichmuth admits. "Sometimes I'd spend weeks feeling stuck, second-guessing decisions or worrying about what went wrong. That paralysis often became a bigger problem than the original mistake." "Admitting what you don't know is actually one of the most valuable things you can do." Over time, learning to absorb those blows became Weatherman's greatest catalyst for growth. Today, Reichmuth caps his frustration at a few hours before pivoting back to problem-solving. "Admitting what you don't know is actually one of the most valuable things you can do," he says. "Once you accept that failure is normal — not something to be ashamed of — it becomes a whole lot easier to keep moving forward." The sun comes out The ultimate validation didn't come from TV ratings; it came on the crowded sidewalks of New York. "I'd be walking around and suddenly see someone carrying one of our umbrellas," Reichmuth says. "That never gets old." BUILT FROM SCRATCH: HOW A FAMILY TURNED CRAFT BEER INTO A HOLIDAY TRADITION The sweetest moments, however, are the ones where customers praise the gear without any idea who he is. "They hadn't bought it because they'd seen me on television," he points out. "They bought it because a friend recommended it, or they discovered it online, or they'd heard it was a great umbrella." For an entrepreneur who started by tearing apart umbrellas in his apartment, earning that pure, organic trust was everything. Today, with Weatherman expanding and solidly profitable over the last few years, the journey has more than paid off. Staying dry What separates Weatherman from the sea of disposable umbrellas? Engineering. Armed with heavy-duty fiberglass frames and water-repellent recycled fabric, the canopies are wind-tunnel tested to withstand gusts of up to 55 mph. They double as sun protection with built-in UPF 50+, and feature smooth auto-open mechanisms to spare users the classic rain-soaked struggle. CEO SUNDAY: ATOMIC WINGS CEO SHARES HIS JOURNEY FROM WALL STREET TO THE RESTAURANT BUSINESS But the true differentiator is how Weatherman approaches design: by use case. Recognizing that a city commuter has different needs than a backcountry hiker or a weekend golfer, the brand organizes its lineup into distinct categories like Walk, Trek, Travel, Golf and Kids — outfitting each with specialized features like reflective trim or pocket-friendly sizing to match real-world habits. Rainbow on the horizon Today, Weatherman has expanded into sun shirts and ponchos for adults, kids and even pets — designed for real-life moments like youth soccer games or unexpected vacation downpours. Recognizing that not everyone wants to splurge on rain gear they hope to rarely use, Reichmuth and his team are developing a more affordable sister brand. Set to debut in 2027, it will bring Weatherman's signature thoughtful engineering to a wider, budget-conscious audience. Still, one thing is for sure: Forecasts aren’t always certain, but Reichmuth’s goal is to help people stay prepared when conditions take an unexpected turn. articles.title: Insiders Reveal 49ers’ Asking Price to Vikings for Mac Jones
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings were looking everywhere for a QB leading up to the 4 pm Nov. 10 trade deadline. Eventually, they were able to trade a 2027 third-round...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings were looking everywhere for a QB leading up to the 4 pm Nov. 10 trade deadline. Eventually, they were able to trade a 2027 third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders for Kirk Cousins.

Nonetheless, the Vikings were looking at every option to find a QB who could get their offense trending in the right direction midway through the season. One of the names that Minnesota called about was the San Francisco 49ers' Mac Jones.

On Nov. 14, ESPN NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported what the Niners were demanding from the Vikings to trade Jones to a potential NFC opponent in the playoffs.

"When the Vikings called San Francisco as part of due diligence in their search for a quarterback, sources told ESPN that Niners general manager John Lynch informed Minnesota brass that it would take a second-round pick and more for Jones," the insiders wrote in their report.

"Perhaps a second-rounder and a middle-round pick might have gotten a trade done. Instead, because of the high cost associated with the veteran quarterback, the conversations ended there and Jones remains a valued member of the 49ers."

The Niners likely view Jones as an important insurance policy should Brock Purdy get hurt, as last season he showed that he can steady the ship if an injury does happen. Jones has a passer rating of 97.4 with 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns, and six interceptions in 13 games for the 49ers, per StatMuse .

Kirk Cousins' Transition Back to Vikings Offense Going Well

Meanwhile, ESPN NFL senior reporter Jeremy Fowler shared an update on Cousins' transition back into the Vikings offense after being away for three years.

"It was as smooth as can be," Fowler said during a Nov. 14 appearance on "SportsCenter." "Remember, he's got six teammates in the starting offensive line depth chart right now that it's sort of too familiar for him. But the first thing he did, I was told, when he got there was get with his center, Blake Brandel, to just get through the snaps and make sure they have the same cadence on the play action under center. We got to work on that. They feel like he's throwing the ball well.

"Kevin O'Connell's added some wrinkles in his offense throughout the years since Cousins has been there, but it remains mostly intact. So they feel like it's been as good as it could have gone for a short three-day window for him to literally come into town on a Wednesday, prep for three days, and be the starter."

KOC Isn't Looking to Overwhelm Kirk Cousins

Nonetheless, while Cousins' transition back into the Vikings' offense has reportedly been smooth, head coach Kevin O'Connell isn't looking to overwhelm the veteran as he shared an update on how they are getting the veteran QB comfortable for the Week 10 game against the Green Bay Packers .

"He believes wholeheartedly in what we do and his role in moving the team," O'Connell told reporters on Nov. 13 . "So really, it's about getting the plan working with him and getting him the plan in real time, in many ways, play by play, situation by situation, and then letting him digest it and getting back together and talking through things post-install, post-reps in practice.

"We'll spend some time together [on Nov. 13] and use every moment we have up until the game. But I'm really looking forward to seeing him play. Though it's something we've always known about him, the way he threw the football this week was a really cool thing to see."

articles.title: Despite Praise, Shifty WR Must Wait to Make Steelers Debut
articles.summary: Max Hurleman‘s name popped up as one to watch this week as the Pittsburgh Steelers prepared for Sunday night’s AFC […]
articles.body:
Max Hurleman 's name popped up as one to watch this week as the Pittsburgh Steelers prepared for Sunday night's AFC North road matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.

Despite the votes of confidence from Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers, the second-year receiver won't be making his NFL debut just yet.

"I mean, how do you not love Max (Hurelman)? McCarthy said Thursday. "I mean, Max is, he's one of the guys you, as a new coach, new coaching staff. You come in here every day doing everything right. GPS was, [he] burned it up. I mean, just, the guy has an incredible workload capacity, work ethic, so unfortunate that he got hurt when he did. I felt that he truly performed to a level that he deserved a 53-man roster spot. So, it'll be great to get him back and get him back into the fold."

Hurleman played collegiately at Colgate before transferring to Notre Dame. He stuck with the Steelers after a rookie minicamp tryout, then spent the entirety of his rookie season on the practice squad without being elevated.

Hurleman had three receptions for 46 yards in the Steelers' 28-9 preseason win over the Green Bay Packers.

articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau Builds His Legacy Back Home In Clovis
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau unveils an 18-hole course and homes in Clovis, California. The two-time major champ reinvests his LIV earnings into his hometown roots.
articles.body:
Bryson DeChambeau is building an 18-hole golf course and a residential community right in his hometown of Clovis, California, according to Billionaires.Africa . The two-time U.S. Open champion announced this massive project on Friday, November 13. He plans to turn the historic McFarlane Ranch into a hub for golf and living.

The project covers about 200 acres on the northeastern edge of Fresno. DeChambeau expects the city to approve the plan within 18 months. He told reporters that a significant portion of his LIV Golf earnings is being allocated to finance this development. His contract with the Saudi-backed league was widely reported at about $125 million when he joined in 2022. That financial backing allows him to reshape his local landscape without waiting for outside investors.

Most golf stars chase fame in big cities like Los Angeles or Miami. DeChambeau is doing the opposite by investing in a city of about 120,000 people. He grew up in Clovis and attended Clovis East High School before turning pro. The plan pairs the new golf course with homes for people to buy. It creates a long-term legacy rather than a quick profit flip.

With five LIV Golf titles to his name, DeChambeau has secured nine victories during his PGA Tour career. He also has two major championships to his name. His scientific approach to the game made him one of the most talked-about players ever. Now he is applying that same focus to building a community. His academic path included studying physics at Southern Methodist University, where he claimed the 2015 NCAA individual title. That same drive for precision is now being used to design a course and a neighborhood.

On his YouTube channel, DeChambeau boasts a subscriber count exceeding three million. His fame in content creation matches the renown he has achieved through his competitive career. While other players focus on social media clips, he is building something you can walk on. The Head Professional at Sugarloaf Golf Club, Oscar Parks, said DeChambeau is very down to earth. Parks noted that the group did not have a ton of lists or demands during their time together.

"They were very professional and they didn't waste a lot of time," Parks explained in an interview. He further noted that the group consisted entirely of ordinary guys. This attitude fits the Clovis project perfectly. DeChambeau does not need a fancy clubhouse to prove his worth. He needs a place where he can play and build with people he knows.

articles.title: Packers Get Encouraging Update on RB’s Injury as Return Timeline Emerges
articles.summary: Riding 6-3 momentum after a dominant 45-27 win over the New England Patriots, the Green Bay Packers enter a crucial Week 10 NFC North clash against the Minne...
articles.body:
Riding 6-3 momentum after a dominant 45-27 win over the New England Patriots, the Green Bay Packers enter a crucial Week 10 NFC North clash against the Minnesota Vikings with a major question mark in their backfield.

But last Sunday, Josh Jacobs broke his right ring finger in the first quarter. While the star back has already been ruled out ahead of Green Bay's Week 11 bye, the team just received an encouraging update regarding how long he will actually be sidelined.

Josh Jacobs' finger surgery update and recovery timeline

Jacobs injured his hand while trying to stiff-arm Patriots defensive back Craig Woodson near the sideline in the first quarter, finishing with just four carries for five yards and a fumble before heading to the locker room.

Having played just three games this season after missing the first six on the Commissioner's Exempt List, the veteran running back leaves a noticeable void in Matt LaFleur's offense.

Earlier in the week, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Jacobs could return in as little as two to three weeks following the procedure. On Saturday, Tom Pelissero confirmed that Jacobs underwent successful surgery on Friday, Nov. 13, in Los Angeles and "should be back in the next few weeks."

Because an injured reserve stint requires a mandatory four-game absence, Green Bay opted against placing Jacobs on IR ahead of Sunday's matchup. Since the Week 11 bye gives him extra recovery time without missing another game, he has a chance to return as early as Week 12 against the Los Angeles Rams on Thanksgiving Eve or Week 13 against the New Orleans Saints.

With the three-time Pro Bowler sidelined, second-year running back Kaleb Johnson is the top candidate to lead Green Bay's backfield against Minnesota. After Jacobs exited in Week 9, Johnson delivered the Packers' best rushing performance of the season with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown.

The Athletic's Matt Schneidman also noted that Green Bay should depend heavily on Johnson over MarShawn Lloyd. Alongside Lloyd, Pierre Strong Jr. and Chris Brooks are also available on the roster, giving LaFleur multiple options to keep the offense balanced while Jacobs recovers through the bye.

articles.title: 3 things on Packers defense vs. Vikings: Cisse vs. Jefferson Part 2
articles.summary: Brandon Cisse gets a chance to show his growth in his second matchup with Justin Jefferson after a 'welcome to the NFL' moment back in Week 1.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers defense is looking for redemption after giving up 39 points to Minnesota back in Week 1, and they will now face a new quarterback at Lambeau Field on Sunday after the Vikings traded for old friend Kirk Cousins.

Many of the points surrendered in the season opener came off turnovers which put Minnesota in the red zone, and one touchdown drive was heavily aided by some baffling officiating Jonathan Gannon's unit will want to show that what happened in Week 1 was a fluke.

Here are three thoughts on the matchup between the Packers defense and the Vikings offense.

Cousins will elevate the Vikings offense

Minnesota had to do something at quarterback with the uninspiring combination of Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz threatening to waste an elite defense as the offense ranked 28th in expected points added (EPA) per pass and 29th in passing success rate.

Kirk Cousins should be a legitimate upgrade over the previous options. His numbers are not gaudy, but he was playing good ball for a Raiders offense lacking talent, ranking 11th in EPA per pass and 8th in success rate. He is in the top half of the league in a lot of different metrics.

The Vikings' offensive line is solid, allowing the 9th lowest pressure rate in the league, and Cousins should accentuate that, as he does a great job of getting the ball out, ranking 2nd in pressure-to-sack rate. That will be a big difference from Murray and Wentz, who rank 34th and 40th.

Green Bay will be hoping to catch Cousins at a good time as he may take some time getting back up to speed in Kevin O'Connell's defense having only arrived in Minnesota on Tuesday, but there is no doubt his presence makes this a tougher game than it would have been.

Minnesota cannot run the ball, ranking 29th in both EPA/rush and rushing success rate. They will also be without T.J. Hockenson and Jauan Jennings this week, while Jordan Addison is questionable with a thumb injury.

But Cousins will have Justin Jefferson at his disposal, and that might be all he needs. The Packers secondary held Jefferson in check for much of the Week 1 contest, but he got them eventually, putting up a season-high 92 yards and two touchdowns.

That included a 39-yard score against Brandon Cisse who was making his pro debut. It was a 'welcome to the NFL' moment for Cisse, who has gone from strength to strength throughout his rookie season since then, allowing only one more touchdown which came back in Week 2.

Green Bay's corners will need to bring their A-game on Sunday, and the matchup with Jefferson provides Cisse with another opportunity to show what he has learned in the two months since they last met.

The Packers are pretty banged up on defense right now. They will of course be without Edgerrin Cooper and Javon Hargrave who started the Week 1 game against the Vikings, and the status of several other key defenders is up in the air ahead of Sunday's game.

Xavier McKinney popped up on the injury report as a limited practice participant with a foot issue on Friday.

Losing one of the safeties who have been so key to Gannon's defense could be a big problem, and while Javon Bullard told reporters he will play, he is questionable with ankle and knee injuries after only practicing once this week, in a limited capacity on Friday.

Green Bay's pass rush has been effective even without Micah Parsons, albeit aided by Gannon's creativity. Not having Lukas Van Ness – who like Bullard only practiced on Friday and was limited with a back problem – would be a blow as he has been their best edge defender this season.

Elsewhere, it seems Zaire Franklin is one again unlikely to play due to his shin injury, listed as doubtful.

Gannon's group has managed to not really skip a beat despite some key injuries throughout the year so far, but if all of those players are not available against Minnesota, it could have an adverse effect on their ability to hold the Vikings offense down.

articles.title: Golfer Tim O'Neal talks PGA diversity at Phoenix Charles Schwab Cup
articles.summary: Pro golfer Tim O'Neal spoke to The Arizona Republic about his late mom inspiring his career comeback and financing for Black golfers.
articles.body:
Tim O'Neal had a calm smile during his practice shots at the Phoenix Country Club. Clad in his crisp blue long-sleeve shirt and Servpro badge, white hat and matching shorts, O'Neal was in the Valley competing in his third straight Charles Schwab Cup Championship, Nov. 12-15.

O'Neal was among 36 qualifiers for the PGA Tour Champions season finale. He is the lone African-American competing for his first title.

"Hopefully, other golfers of color will realize and see if I can do it, they can do it too," O'Neal told The Arizona Republic earlier this week.

O'Neal is approaching nearly 30 years as a pro and fourth PGA Tour Champions season. He started on the Korn Ferry Tour as a rookie in 1997 out of Jackson State University, a rarity for a player from a historically Black college or university (HBCU). That was the same year Tiger Woods turned pro and became the first African-American to win the Masters.

Since then, golf diversity has reached an all-time high of 25%, or seven million, among Black, Asian, or Latinx players in 2024, up from 8% in 1990, per the National Golf Foundation (NGF) and United States Golf Association (USGA).

Black pro golfers also on the current tour include Harold Varner II, Joseph Bramlett and Cameron Champ.

"With Tiger getting on tour, winning majors and dominating for a long time, that definitely I would think has had an effect," O'Neal said.

O'Neal, 52, has had a strong 2026, with five top-10 finishes through 27 events. And he's still riding the coattails of his sole career victory at the Dominion Energy Charity Classic in October 2024.

See final round of 2026 WM Phoenix Open in photos

That's a turnaround from the multiple heartbreaks at qualifying school (Q-school) earlier in his career. He missed earning his PGA Tour card twice by one stroke in 2001 and 2004, before finally securing it in 2008.

"You get a little smarter, course management's a little bit better," O'Neal said. "Probably in my younger days probably a little more aggressive on the course. I'm now a bit more conservative. ... But once I got on the Champions Tour, I think for me I still need some more work, but short game was the main thing. I've improved there but I still have some room to grow there as well and just getting more comfortable with these guys out here, some of the best players in the world."

O'Neal was sponsored by actor and hip hop legend Will Smith earlier in his career. The loss of his PGA card, Nationwide Tour privileges and lack of money nearly caused O'Neal to quit for good.

From 2010-11, O'Neal worked and gave lessons at Edwin Watts golf shop in his native Savannah, Georgia, while he played in mini tournaments over the next two years. His late mother Eva O'Neal, who passed away in 2020, urged him to stick with the game that she and his dad taught him to play.

In 2013, O'Neal played in the eGOLF Tour in Charlotte, which helped jump-start his career. He then went to Morocco in the Moroccan Golf Federation and played six tournaments and earned $7,500 in each of his three wins. He continued to fund his own comeback as that prize money got him into another bigger European tournament, Trophy Hassan II, and he won $18,000 by finishing in the top 20.

Then got into Q-school at the PGA Tour Latinoamérica in South America in 2013. Then, in 2014, he played again on the Korn Ferry tour.

"Twenty-something years ago, you could probably skimp here and skimp there to find a way to get through, but now it's impossible," O'Neal told The Arizona Republic. "Everyone's good, everyone has the best coaches and best courses to play, and it's sad to say this but if you don't have financial backing, you really don't have a chance. And it costs about $100,000 a year to really do it the right way."

Many Black amateur golfers face the same issue to develop and become pros, especially those from HBCUs.

Jackson State put a two-year suspension on its men's and women's golf program as part of the university's $106 million budget cuts, that included travel spending, in 2017. After a protracted hiatus, which O'Neal called "sad" for the former "powerhouse in golf," Jackson State resumed its program in 2025.

In addition, there are PGA events and programs such as the APGA Tour , Pathway To Progression and Coca-Cola partnership with the PGA Tour for the HBCU Golf Impact Grant, which pledges $250,000 to 10 partner schools and 16 golf programs.

Lucrative college NIL deals and allocation mostly goes to more popular college sports such as basketball and football.

"If it wasn't for the people who helped me along the way to get here now, unless you come from a wealthy family, very expensive sport to play with equipment and all the stuff you need to really make it,'' O'Neal said. "These financial groups, whatever they can do to help golfers get to the next level, you need it because there's very few golfers who made it that didn't have backing behind them."

articles.title: Trump takes parting shot at DC golf course conditions one day before major overhaul begins
articles.summary: Trump shared photos of what he calls "Trash Island" on Truth Social, blasting U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes for slowing the East Potomac overhaul.
articles.body: A day before a D.C. golf course is set to close for a major overhaul under President Donald Trump, the president took one more chance to take a shot at its apparently poor conditions. In May, the National Links Trust announced that the Trump administration will be giving East Potomac Golf Links, a public D.C. course, a "historic restoration." The project has faced roadblocks, including U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes saying she would open a "formal inquiry" to investigate if attorneys for the Trump administration violated ethical boundaries during a legal dispute about the project. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Trump said the course, which he called "Trash Island," is the "worst" in the world, "but the Department of the Interior is going to make it into the Best Golf Course anywhere in the World." "Unfortunately, Judge Ana Reyes doesn’t want us to quickly and inexpensively fix up the Course," Trump said in a Saturday Truth Social post. Trump also said the conditions of the course are "very dangerous," adding pictures of what appears to be the course in poor shape. "The Fairways are far too close together. When you walk down the corridors of Trash Island, you don’t hear the sound of the running Potomac, all you hear is the sound of people screaming, 'FORE!'," Trump wrote. SPORTS WORLD REACTS TO THE SUDDEN PASSING OF LEGENDARY BROADCASTER DAN HICKS AT THE AGE OF 64 "In any event, we’re making progress, and hopefully the Judge will agree that the Dignity, Beauty, and Importance of Washington, D.C., will be greatly enhanced by this soon to be beautiful Project. Trash Island, after years of laughter and scorn, will evolve into something very special, something which the Judge will be able to take great pride in seeing! All over the World it will be acclaimed as being the Best Golf Course anywhere." Trump said the course will have the potential to host major golf tournaments, including the U.S. Open, the PGA Championship, the Ryder Cup and the Presidents Cup, and D.C.-area residents will be able to play for half off. The course, located along the Potomac River near the National Mall, will be redesigned by Tom Fazio. It sits on federally owned land at East Potomac Park and has been part of Washington's public golf scene for more than a century. Reyes recently temporarily halted additional tree cutting amid a legal challenge over work at the property. Fox News' Amanda Macias and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Tiger Woods, Jack Nicklaus pay tribute to Dan Hicks as golf remembers iconic NBC broadcaster
articles.summary: Tiger Woods and Jack Nicklaus have joined the golf world in remembering Dan Hicks, the longtime NBC Sports broadcaster who died at 64.
articles.body: Tiger Woods and Jack Nicklaus have joined the golf world in remembering Dan Hicks, the longtime NBC Sports broadcaster who died at 64. Woods shared a personal tribute after the news of Hicks’ death, recalling a friendship that grew beyond the golf course. Hicks will also be remembered for his call during Woods’ dramatic 2008 U.S. Open run at Torrey Pines. As Woods sank the birdie putt that forced a playoff with Rocco Mediate, Hicks delivered the line, “Expect anything different?” It became one of golf broadcasting’s best-known calls and stayed with fans for years.Tiger Woods remembers his friend Dan Hicks after the broadcaster’s deathHicks died in Connecticut on November 11 after an acute illness. His wife, ESPN broadcaster Hannah Storm, announced his death the following day. They had been married for more than 30 years and had three daughters: Hannah, Ellery and Riley.Woods shared his tribute on X on November 13. He remembered Hicks as a close friend both on and off the golf course.“Dan Hicks was beloved by all who had the privilege of knowing and working alongside him. His kindness, warmth, and presence will be deeply missed.“Like so many in the golf world, Dan was a great friend to me both on and off the course. I had the utmost respect for him and the incredible job he did for our sport for decades. Our thoughts are with Hannah and their daughters during this incredibly difficult time.“I hope they find comfort in knowing how much he meant to so many people and the lasting impact he made on everyone whose life he touched,” Woods wrote.Their connection was linked to one of golf’s most memorable days. Woods was playing the 2008 U.S. Open with a torn ACL and two stress fractures in his left tibia. He was in pain and at times used his club for support. At the 18th hole, he needed a birdie to tie Rocco Mediate.When the putt dropped, Woods raised both fists as the Torrey Pines crowd roared. Hicks later said on GOLF.com’s “Off Course with Claude Harmon” that his famous line was not planned. He was thinking about the people around the green and the millions watching at home. He felt they all expected Woods to make the putt. The words came to him as the ball went in.Jack Nicklaus remembers his friendship with Dan HicksNicklaus also paid tribute to Hicks, recalling the many interviews and conversations they shared. In a message on Instagram, the 18-time major champion called him a good friend and said their interviews felt more like conversations between old friends. He praised Hicks as a gentleman and a professional, and sent his condolences to Storm and their daughters.Hicks joined NBC Sports in 1992 after working in local television and at CNN. He became the network’s lead golf play-by-play announcer in 2000. The Associated Press reported that he called 27 of Woods’ tournament victories, along with major golf events and Ryder Cups.Born and raised in Tucson, Hicks graduated from Sabino High School in 1980 and earned a journalism degree from the University of Arizona in 1984. He worked in local radio and television before joining CNN in 1989, where he met Storm.Golf was a major part of his work, but Hicks also covered Olympic swimming and skiing, Notre Dame football and other sports.Woods’ message showed that their bond went far beyond the famous call. articles.title: The Annika: Lottie Woad in the mix as Lindy Duncan edges closer to first-ever LPGA Tour victory
articles.summary: Lindy Duncan took the 54-hole lead at The Annika; she is out to win her first LPGA Tour title; Lottie Woad is six shots back while Charley Hull struggled on day three; Watch round four of The Annika on LPGA Tour from 7pm on Sunday, live on Sky Sports Mix
articles.body:
On a cold and blustery day at Pelican Golf Club, the 35-year-old, who joined the tour in 2014, took the 54-hole lead by shooting a four-under 69.

Overnight co-leader Hye-Jin Choi was tied at the top until she missed the 18th green to the left but did well to get down in three for a bogey and a 70, and finished one stroke back from Duncan.

England's Lottie Woad tied a group of six players - including world No 1 Nelly Korda - at seven under par, with the European Solheim Cup player twinning two birdies and two bogeys to wrap up her day at level par.

Charley Hull endured a difficult day, with the 30-year-old posting six bogeys to finish with a 76 and fall down to tied-43rd on the leaderboard at one under par.

Yuri Yoshida, who won her first LPGA title during the recent Asia swing, played alongside Korda and had a 67, leaving her two shots off the lead.

Ina Yoon of South Korea (69) was three behind and double major winner Haeran Ryo went from eight shots behind to four back with a Saturday-low 65.

Duncan, who made her debut at the Solheim Cup at age 35 and is making her 222nd career start on the LPGA Tour without winning, was at 13-under 197. The American's lone birdie came at the par-four 11th hole, after striking a seven-iron to 18 feet.

Her final act was 50ft putt over a green that looked more like bunny slopes, three ridges to cover. Duncan nearly holed it and then rapped in a 3-footer for a par to polish off a clean card.

"Today was a really tough day with the wind," Duncan said.

"The greens firm up, so I was really just trying to hit the ball in spots where you could at least hit the green or have a reasonable chip."

Greens are the defence at Pelican Golf Club, and some of the pins were in their toughest positions. Carlota Ciganda, who shared the 54-hole lead with Choi and Duncan, three-putted five times, including the 18th.

That was a big help to Duncan, who was roughly on the same line as Ciganda.

"I also thought she hit it a lot harder and it didn't go that far past, so I definitely think seeing her putt helped make mine a little easier," Duncan said.

"For that one to kind of skim the edge was pretty cool."

The 18th took a toll on just about everyone, playing all the way back into the wind.

World No 1 Nelly Korda also struggled in the trying conditions.

Korda three-putted down the ridge on the 18th for a bogey that gave her a 71 and left her six shots behind. A win can see the world No 1 qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame.

She wasn't at her best on Saturday. The 28-year-old took a double bogey on the sixth hole by going over the green into the pine straw, chipping down a ridge and off the green, taking three to get down from there.

On her back nine, Korda carded two birdies and two bogeys, also coming unstuck on the par-four 18th.

Along with trying to win, Duncan still is not eligible for the season-ending CME Group Tour Championship next week, where the winner of the top 60 players who qualify gets £1.5m ($2m). A strong finish, even without winning, gets her there.

Choi has no such concerns about the season finale. She just wants to win, and two runner-up finishes during the Asia swing have helped her confidence.

"I'm just going to try to concentrate to the end," Choi said.

articles.title: Seeking first PGA Tour win, Trace Crowe takes solo lead into Sunday at Austin Championship
articles.summary: Trace Crowe has just 50 starts on the PGA Tour, but he knows no one can coast to the finish line.
articles.body:
Trace Crowe has just 50 starts on the PGA Tour, but he knows no one can coast to the finish line in this sport.

"I've been doing this long enough to know that everyone's really good and they're just going to keep making birdies," Crowe said Saturday. "My mindset tomorrow is to go attack the day and see what it gives, but just try to play the best I can and hopefully it come out on top."

Crowe has been attacking the Fazio Canyons Course at Omni Barton Creek resort all week, and he'll take the solo lead into the final round at the 2026 Austin Championship , where he seeks his first PGA Tour victory.

Playing in the final group in Saturday's third round, Crowe started with a birdie at the first, but back-to-back bogeys at Nos. 3 and 4 and again at Nos. 10 and 11 set him back. He offset them with birdies at the fifth, ninth and 14th, then finished strong with two more birdies on the final two holes to cap off a 1-under 71, getting him to 14 under for the tournament, one shot clear of a three-way tie for second.

"[It was] very difficult. Just being in that position just in the final group and, you know, made a nice putt on 1 to get it going, then got smacked in the face on 3 and 4, and then it was pretty much head down for the rest of the day, just kind of up and down round. Yeah, really pleased with the last two."

Crowe is a two-time winner on the Korn Ferry Tour, but he's never tasted victory in the big leagues. He's not treating the Austin Championship any differently, though.

"I think [my game plan is] just keep doing what I'm doing," Crowe said. "Just got to drive it on the fairway. Like you said, it's going to be challenging tomorrow. I think just kind of keeping your head down, being patient and just seeing where it puts us at the end. Have to make a few putts.

One of the men just one shot off the lead is Erik van Rooyen, who shot 3-under 69 Saturday to put himself in a tie for second with Chad Ramey and Sami Valimaki. Van Rooyen was hot out of the gate in the third round, making four birdies in his first six holes, but stumbled with a bogey at No. 8 and a double bogey at No. 9. He got those strokes back with birdies at Nos. 12, 14 and 18.

"Yeah, pretty upset about the double on 9. For me, that was such a difficult shot, I had to take some off a 6-iron and try and draw it. Left's no good. Obviously it's better than hitting in the water, I understand, but I tried to just hit a little draw that would hold into the wind, and ball below my feet started right. But yeah, to keep the emotions in check, my caddie just kind of whispered, like you know you're playing great. Knowing that in the back of your mind makes it easier making the turn."

Valimaki, meanwhile, is just a week removed from defending his title at the RSM Classic in Georgia next week.

"I don't know what is all about in this kind of late, but I feel like I've been playing many years now pretty good later in the season. It's nice to show it up."

Valimaki and Ramey will join the solo leader, Crowe, in the final group Sunday, teeing off at 10:01 a.m. ET.

articles.title: Federal judge blocks Trump's renovations of DC golf course hours before its closure
articles.summary: A federal judge cited Donald Trump's Truth Social posts as key evidence when issuing a temporary restraining order on the East Potomac renovation.
articles.body: A federal judge issued a temporary restraining order Saturday to delay closing a D.C.-area golf course amid President Donald Trump's push to have the course renovated. U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued the two-week delay before the East Potomac Golf Links was due to close Sunday for 15 months. The course sits on federally owned land at East Potomac Park and has been part of Washington's public golf scene for more than a century. Trump announced in May the course would undergo a "historic renovation" that would prepare it to host major professional golf events. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The plaintiffs argue that Trump's plan would change the character of the accessible golf course and make it unaffordable, something the president denies. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Trump has dubbed the course "Trash Island," doing so as recently on Saturday in a Truth Social post in which he said it is the "worst" course in the world. Trump said the conditions of the course are "very dangerous," adding pictures of what appears to be the course in poor shape. "The Fairways are far too close together. When you walk down the corridors of Trash Island, you don’t hear the sound of the running Potomac, all you hear is the sound of people screaming, 'FORE!'," Trump wrote. Trump has posted about the course in the past. Reyes in her ruling Saturday noted that Trump's posts presented a problem for the government. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER "They indicate that the Washington National Plan is final and that [National Park Service] will close the Park to implement it," she wrote. "Both points favor granting Plaintiffs’ motion for another temporary restraining order." The park’s redevelopment is one of multiple projects in the nation's capital that Trump has championed to remake the city. They include a large memorial arch, a White House ballroom and the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, among others. Reyes, who was nominated to the court by Joe Biden, had for months been reticent about approving the plaintiffs’ requests for work stoppages. The plaintiffs had argued the administration was moving ahead with work related to the project despite the pending lawsuit. Her reluctance to issue orders ended in October, spurred in part by a tree-cutting spree by the administration over a holiday weekend with little notification to the judge or plaintiffs. Officials and government lawyers said the tree work was part of a 2019 plan that recommended the cutting. In response, the judge confronted the administration over what she portrayed as deceitful actions over its intentions for the project. Reyes has repeatedly expressed frustration over the minute planning details she has been asked to adjudicate, including over the trees being cut down at the 106-year-old park. articles.title: Judge temporarily blocks Trump from closing Washington DC golf course for renovation
articles.summary: It is the latest development in a months-long challenge to the US president's plans for East Potomac Golf Links.
articles.body:
A federal judge has temporarily blocked the US government's closure of an historic golf course and park in Washington DC.

US District Judge Ana Reyes has been overseeing a months-long challenge to the president's plans for East Potomac Golf Links, which he said would be closed from 15 November for extensive renovations.

Reyes has said Donald Trump cannot close the park nor its golf course, but added that his administration was not required to actively manage either.

Trump, an avid golfer, has said his plans to upgrade the 106-year-old course will create "one of the Best and Most Spectacular Golf Courses anywhere in the World". The BBC has contacted the White House for comment.

Declaring the current course "Trash Island", he announced in October that it would be renovated over 15 months to create a space that "will be open to the Public while, at the same time, designed to the Highest Level of Golf and able to hold World Class Tournaments" - despite the ongoing litigation.

Reyes said in a 30-page decision issued on Saturday that the Trump administration's justifications for the proposed course closures were pretextual and that the government had violated at least two federal laws "to meet an arbitrary deadline".

"The government proposes to close a historic park, daily enjoyed by Washingtonians of all stripes, indefinitely," Reyes wrote.

She said the closure "runs counter to the public interest in utilising national parkland", adding that the government had not "plausibly identified any harm it would suffer from a temporary restraining order that preserves the status quo pending further proceedings".

'Trash Island' or DC landmark? How a golf course got Trump in a messy legal dispute

The legal dispute dates back to February, when the DC Preservation League and others sued over redevelopment plans for the park.

The historic course, which sits two miles (3km) south of the White House, is one of three public courses run by the National Park Service (NPS) in the nation's capital.

The legal fight then escalated in October when the NPS began to cut down hundreds of trees without notifying Reyes until 15 hours before work was set to begin.

After the trees were cut, Reyes ordered the Trump administration to stop tree removal until at least 26 October and give her three business days' notice about making any other permanent changes.

Despite the work stoppage, Trump announced that the course would be closed for 15 months from 15 November to accommodate for the renovations. He also shared a rendering of the course redesign.

"The current Course is old, broken, dilapidated and of no further use or effect. It is in very poor condition, with falling, dangerous and disease-infested trees and, importantly, a collapsing and hazardous seawall," he said in a post on Truth Social.

Reyes has since separately opened an inquiry into whether justice department attorneys had "made misrepresentations to the court and otherwise violated ethical rules".

That included whether giving late notice to the court about the renovation plans had been "done in bad faith", and whether the attorneys failed to correct previously false statements or withheld information.

She said she would carry out the inquiry with a special master, an independent third party.

Hatton took a one-shot lead into the final day at Jumeirah Golf Estates and never relinquished top spot, pulling clear of the field with four birdies in a six-hole stretch on the back nine.

The Englishman posted a six-under 66 to end on 15 under and claim a ninth DP World Tour title, as McIlroy leapfrogged Chacarra in the season-long standings with a runner-up finish after a thrilling Sunday tussle.

McIlroy carded a bogey-free 67 to win the Race to Dubai for a fifth successive season and match Colin Montgomerie's record of eight Order of Merit titles, with Chacarra narrowly missing out despite sharing third with a three-under 69.

Chacarra ended the week on eight under alongside Oliver Lindell, both among the 10 players to have secured dual membership on the PGA Tour via their Race to Dubai ranking, with Jacob Skov Olesen, Kristoffer Reitan, Francesco Laporta, Mikael Lindberg and Victor Perez all a further shot back in tied-fifth.

How McIlroy made history during Hatton's Dubai win

Hatton scrambled an unlikely par at the first after having to punch out from the trees, which double his lead when Perez made bogey, then quickly grabbed control with back-to-back birdies from the second.

McIlroy - starting four back - opened with a birdie but missed further chances over the front nine, only to race within one of Hatton after three birdies in a four-hole burst from the sixth.

Chacarra made a three-birdie run from the sixth to sit one back alongside Race to Dubai rival McIlroy and Lindberg, who briefly pulled level with Hatton after four birdies in his opening eight holes.

McIlroy reclaimed projected top spot in the season-long standings when Chacarra posted back-to-back bogeys around the turn, with the pair flip-flopping between the two spots during an eventful back nine.

Chacarra responded to another bogey at the 12th by birdieing his next two holes, briefly edging ahead by 0.1 projected points, with McIlroy visibly frustrated after starting his back nine with pars and failing to take advantage of the par-five 14th.

The battle for the Race to Dubai was far closer than the title race, as Hatton posted birdies at the 10th and 12th before extending his buffer with back-to-back gains from the 14th to jump five ahead.

McIlroy reclaimed the lead over Chacarra in the rankings with a stunning birdie at the 16th and pars over his last two holes, with another Harry Vardon Trophy confirmed when nobody could move alongside him on 10 under.

Hatton got up and down to save par at the 17th and closed out victory with a par at the last, seeing him go one better than last week's runner-up finish at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship and claim a sixth Rolex Series title.

Chacarra 'proud' of Race to Dubai fight with McIlroy

Rory McIlroy, on his runner-up finish and eighth Race to Dubai: "Winning eight Order of Merits was never in my list of goals when I was growing up! I remember Monty [Colin Montgomerie] being a stalwart of European golf.

"To pull up alongside him and win eight of these things means the world to me. I'm a very proud European, I'm a proud European player, I'm proud to be part of the DP World Tour and I'm very proud of myself right now."

Eugenio Chacarra, on missing out on the Race to Dubai : "It was a good fight. I just came out short - that's the beauty of golf. He [McIlroy] has played here 14, 15 times, it was going to be tough, and he had a better day than I did.

"I knew it was going to be a long day and I tried my best. That's all I can ask for myself to do and that's what we did. I would say proud of the fight and proud to have a chance till the end."

Tyrrell Hatton, following his tournament victory : "I was really nervous today, I didn't really say anything to any of my team or even to Emily [partner].

"I've had a bit of heartbreak around here and I felt like it was going to be a difficult day. I'm just really proud of how I played on the back nine. The putter was amazing; it certainly saved me all week. It feels so good to win here."

The new DP World Tour season begins at the BMW Australian PGA Championship from November 26-29, held at The Lakes GC in Sydney.

articles.standfirst: El norirlandés conquista su octava Orden de Mérito e iguala el récord de Colin Montgomerie tras ser segundo en Dubái. Chacarra acaba tercero, pero no le basta para reinar
articles.summary: El norirlandés conquista su octava Orden de Mérito e iguala el récord de Colin Montgomerie tras ser segundo en Dubái. Chacarra acaba tercero, pero no le basta para reinar
articles.body: Eugenio López-Chacarra (69) se quedó a un par de golpes de reinar en el DP World Tour, de añadir su nombre a los de Jon Rahm y Seve Ballesteros. Le faltaron 125 puntos. Su lucha, su empeño y su trabajo durante 31 torneos esta temporada quedará en la memoria. Se le abren las puertas de un futuro interesante: el PGA Tour, jugar los cuatro grandes... Para lo que se preparó en los dos últimos años. Rory McIlroy (67 golpes), mientras, se coronó por octava vez. Acabó segundo en solitario, tras Tyrrell Hatton, sumando los puntos suficientes para rebasar al español. Iguala en el histórico del European Tour de toda la vida a Colin Montgomerie. Con sólo 12 presencias en todo el curso le ha bastado una vez más para reinar. (Resultados) Chacarra y McIlroy se liaron a tiros desde el inicio. El día, apenas brisa, invitaba a ello. Rory empezó con birdie los nueve primeros hoyos y los abrochó con otro acierto. Los jugó en 32 golpes. Eugenio, de naranja, con los colores de Oklahoma State, ritual de domingo, fabricó un -3 gracias a un estupendo momento con los hierros. Enlazó tres birdies seguidos (6, 7 y 8), secuencia que se vio frenada por un bogey en el 9. Hatton y Lindberg, también acertados, eran dos buenos aliados para el español en ese momento porque bloqueaban las dos primeras plazas al norirlandés. Ese error de Chacarra se tradujo en momentos de dudas. La pegó atrás desde la calle en el 10 y cayó otro bogey. Y otro más en el 12. McIlroy, que había disfrutado sólo de seis minutos del liderato de la Race to Dubái, hasta ese momento, se veía de nuevo arriba. Era un escenario propicio al lucimiento: Ángel Ayora acababa de jugar los nueve segundos hoyos en 28 golpes (6 birdies y un eagle) para un 64. Chacarra reaccionó con el quinto birdie del día en el 13. Ha hecho 25 esta semana, más que nadie. Sacó el puño. Fue el momento que necesitaba para espolearse. McIlroy, unos metros por delante, no sacó partido al par 5 del 14 y el español vio el momento. Embocó el segundo birdie y recobró el liderato en la Orden de Mérito ¡por sólo una décima! a falta de cuatro hoyos. Después de 2.084 hoyos jugados hasta ese instante, le quedaba alcanzar la orilla con éxito, pero un golpe lo podía cambiar todo. Hatton, además, ya tenía muy amarrado el título, su sexto Rolex Series, y el primer favor estaba hecho. Quedaba que Lindbeg también fuese un buen socio. McIlroy tiró un dardo en el 16, que le dio el quinto birdie del día. Volvía a encabezar la Orden de Mérito y exigía al español, que escuchó los aplausos desde el centro de la calle de ese tramo. El genio había vuelto. Rory falló la calle del 18 y no consiguió el birdie. Era la primera parte de la ecuación necesaria, pero el resto ya no se descifró bien para los intereses españoles. Lindberg cometió un bogey en el 17 y el reinado de McIlroy sólo lo podían evitar un eagle de Chacarra o del sueco. Eugenio no pasó del par y el nórdico, el último clavo al que agarrarse, la tiró al agua. Larga vida a Rory, que, precavido, no quiso celebrar nada por si Victor Perez, en el último partido, conseguía un albatros.

articles.title: DP World Tour Championship: Rory McIlroy claims Race To Dubai as Tyrell Hatton wins tournament
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy wipes away tears as he dedicates his record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title to his ill father, Gerry.
articles.body:
DP World Tour Championship final leaderboard

15 Hatton (Eng); -10 McIlroy (NI); -8 Chacarra (Spa), Lindell (Fin); -7 Olesen (Den), Reitan (Nor), Laporta (Ita), Lindberg (Swe), Perez (Fra)

Selected others: -4 Wallace (Eng); -3 Rahm (Spa), Schaper (SA); Level Fleetwwod (Eng), Reed (US), Fox (NZ); +1 Rai (Eng)

Rory McIlroy wiped away tears as he dedicated his eighth Race to Dubai victory to his ill father, Gerry.

Moments after matching Colin Montgomerie's record of season-long European tour titles on Sunday, the Northern Irishman was asked about the health of his father.

An emotional McIlroy revealed Gerry has been in hospital for two months after "a huge operation" - a double lung transplant - at the end of September.

"He's recovering well, thankfully," McIlroy told the DP World Tour.

"But before I left to come here to the Middle East, I went up to Cleveland to see him. He said to me: 'Go win The Race to Dubai'.

It came after a thrilling climax at the traditional season-ending DP World Tour Championship with Tyrrell Hatton securing a commanding victory, while McIlroy pipped Spaniard Eugenio Chacarra to the overall crown.

Hatton's closing six-under-par 66 helped him romp to a five-shot victory on 15 under par but most eyes were on the thrilling battle that went down to the final hole.

It is the fifth successive year that McIlroy has won the award and it has drawn him level with Montgomerie, the Scot who set a mark 21 years ago that few thought would ever be matched.

"Yeah, double digits," smiled McIlroy when asked what would be his final target of Race to Dubai victories.

"I'd love to surpass Monty next year and we'll go from there."

McIlroy's confidence in going along with a target shouted out by the fans surrounding the 18th green at the Earth Course in Dubai on Sunday was refreshing to hear.

But he appears to be playing and talking with a little more freedom in recent years - the sort of freedom that comes as a result of finally completing the career Grand Slam and winning successive Masters titles - and leads to declarations of winning 10, or more.

"Winning eight Order of Merits (Race to Dubai titles) was never in my list of goals growing up," said McIlroy, who closed with a bogey-free 67 to finish on 10 under and must surely now be considered Europe's greatest golfer.

"I remember Monty being a stalwart of the European tour and playing with him at the London Club in 2008, so to pull up alongside him and win eight of these means the world to me."

After Jon Rahm's victory in Abu Dhabi last week, fellow former LIV Golf member Hatton showed his class with a five-shot success at the Earth Course at Jumeirah Golf Estates.

Hatton showed his combustible side earlier in the week but, despite later admitting to being "weirdly nervous" he appeared serene on Sunday.

In the final group and knowing he couldn't win the overall Race to Dubai title, he was detached enough to block out the scramble as he strolled to his ninth DP World Tour victory - even asking an on-course reporter who was going to win as he walked from the 17th green to 18th tee.

It was that head-to-head battle between Chacarra and McIlroy that dominated the tournament, a battle that, after a long hard season, came right down to the wire.

Both players knew victory would win them the title. There were permutations galore for finishing second, third, or below that.

Chacarra and McIlroy went toe-to-toe in and the overall lead in the rankings chopped and changed down an absorbing back nine as neither man backed down.

At one juncture just one-tenth of a point separated the pair.

But a late surge from Northern Ireland's McIlroy allowed him to finish runner-up behind England's Hatton in the tournament and collect enough points to edge out the gutsy Spaniard.

Chacarra, who earned around $15-20m during three years as a LIV player, is in just his second season on the DP World Tour. He is the only three-time winner of this year's campaign and was desperate to add his name to compatriots Rahm and Seve Ballesteros as the third Spanish order of merit winner.

After four early birdies he looked in fine shape. The pressure began to tell as he posted three bogeys in four holes around the turn. But he responded brilliantly with two more birdies to push McIlroy all the way.

Chacarra, the 26-year-old world number 39, finished in a tie for third to end up second in the overall standings and earn a PGA Tour card for next season.

As tough as it was this year for McIlroy to win, mainly due to playing on the PGA Tour for the first half of the season, 2027 will be even harder because there will be some big names flooding in after the collapse of LIV Golf.

Rahm and Hatton are just two high-profile LIV players who are suspended from the PGA Tour for a year following their involvement with the breakaway tour. They will both have a full season on the European circuit that will give them a big advantage over McIlroy.

Along with many other big names such as Sergio Garcia, Joaquin Niemann and Tom McKibbin, there's even the possibility of Bryson DeChambeau, the biggest LIV name of all, applying to join the DP World Tour for next season.

The American is eligible thanks to his 2024 US Open triumph, at McIlroy's painful expense, and had to apply by the end of the Sunday of the DP World Tour Championship.

Is McIlroy Europe's greatest ever golfer?

After this latest addition to McIlroy's glowing CV it's hard to make a case against him being Europe's greatest ever golfer – and as he continues to find new targets to stay motivated one of them is very much to unequivocally nail down that title.

Motivation was a problem in the immediate aftermath of finally ending his long wait to win the Masters in 2025 as he became just the sixth man to win the career Grand Slam.

But a year later he had re-found it as he became just the fourth back-to-back Green Jacket winner with his brilliant defence at Augusta National back in April.

That put him on six major titles, level with England's Sir Nick Faldo and just one behind the great Harry Vardon, whose name adorns the trophy McIlroy has just hoisted for the eighth time.

Still only 37, McIlroy still has plenty of time to overhaul Montgomerie and hold the outright record for the most European number one titles – despite playing on two tours throughout the majority of his career.

Targets have changed – McIlroy is not chasing the world number one spot or winning any old trophy. He's voiced his desire to focus on majors, play more in Europe and around the globe and keep stacking up these order of merit titles.

An Olympic title is perhaps the only honour missing from his trophy cabinet, and he will have the chance to change that in 2028 on a familiar Riviera Country Club Course, which is a regular stop-off on the PGA Tour and where he finished second a this year's Genesis Invitational.

He will be attempting to become the first man to win three Masters in a row next April, before the US Open at Pebble Beach and Open Championship at St Andrews offer great chances at venues McIlroy knows he can thrive on.

McIlroy has won six Ryder Cups as a stalwart for Europe and is just seven points behind all-time leader Sergio Garcia.

But even if the Northern Irishman quit the game right now he's already built a more than compelling argument that he's the greatest player the continent has ever seen.

articles.summary: A runner-up finish in the DP World Tour Championship was enough for Rory McIlroy to secure another Race to Dubai title.
articles.body:
A runner-up finish in the DP World Tour Championship was enough for Rory McIlroy to secure another Race to Dubai title.

He and Colin Montgomerie are now tied for the most Order of Merit awards with eight:

Tyrrell Hatton was the runaway winner of the Tour Championship, finishing five shots ahead of McIlroy at 15 under. The Race to Dubai came down to a head-to-head battle between McIlroy and Eugenio Chacarra.

Chacarra was the season leader heading into the Tour Championship but got overtaken in the finale.

McIlroy kept up the pressure Sunday by saving par on No. 18 after a wayward drive sailed well right of the fairway.

Chacarra wound up tying for third at eight under. His last hope for the Order of Merit came down to Victor Perez, who needed an albatross on the par-five 18th hole. Once Perez's approach came to rest off the green, McIlroy's triumph was official.

McIlroy has achieved basically everything he can as a golfer multiple times over. Still, this Order of Merit felt special.

He said his father had a "huge operation" in September and is still recovering. His dad told him to "Go win the Race to Dubai" when he visited him in the hospital before the event:

Chacarra is left to rue a somewhat slow start to the DP World Tour Championship. He shot an even-par 72 in the opening round and was one-under through 36 holes. That allowed McIlroy to build a five-shot buffer, which was big enough to keep the Spaniard at bay in the final two days.

McIlroy is already looking toward the 2027 season and said he'd "love to surpass Monty next year." A sixth straight Order of Merit will present a formidable challenge, though.

McIlroy, 37, isn't getting any younger, and the DP World Tour is poised to welcome some notable castoffs from LIV Golf, a group that could include Hatton, Jon Rahm and David Puig. The door is open for Bryson DeChambeau as well if he's frozen out from the PGA Tour and wants to play high-level golf.

Hatton was third in the Race to Dubai standings despite only playing in 13 events. Rahm was sixth and only competed in nine DP World Tour tournaments. Having bolted from LIV this past January, Patrick Reed was also a serious contender for McIlroy's crown after playing the circuit while waiting out his PGA Tour suspension.

Depending on how the fallout from LIV Golf's bankruptcy settles, the DP World Tour could have its strongest field for a long time.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy emotional after matching Colin Montgomerie's Race to Dubai record and dedicates win to father in hospital
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy equalled Colin Montgomerie's record of eight DP World Tour Order of Merit titles after claiming the Race to Dubai for a fifth successive season; McIlroy finished runner-up to Tyrrell Hatton at the DP World Tour Championship
articles.body:
The Northern Irishman pipped Eugenio Chacarra to the Harry Vardon Trophy after an eventful final round at Jumeirah Golf Estates, where both players traded top spot in the projected Race to Dubai rankings on multiple occasions before McIlroy claimed the title.

McIlroy secured solo second on 10 under, five strokes behind Ryder Cup team-mate Tyrrell Hatton, ensuring he would top the DP World Tour rankings for a fifth successive season and match Colin Montgomerie's record of eight Order of Merit titles.

The Masters champion revealed that his father has been recovering in hospital following a double-lung transplant in September, with McIlroy in tears as he discussed how much his dad was on his mind during his latest achievement.

"Yeah, a lot," McIlroy admitted. "He has been in the hospital for the last two months. He underwent a huge operation at the end of September and he is recovering well, thankfully.

"When I left to come here to the Middle East, I went up to Cleveland to see him before I went and he said to me, 'Go win the Race to Dubai'. This one is for him."

He later explained his press conference: "It has been a stressful time for our family. I've been up in Cleveland a lot, because that's where he is. I didn't know if I was going to go to India, because I spent nine days in the ICU with him while he was recovering.

"If things were not looking as good as they were, I probably wouldn't have felt comfortable travelling or being too far away. He's got an amazing team up there, and the doctors and nurses are absolutely incredible. So I felt comfortable going to India and travelling and knowing that I could obviously get back to him if I needed to.

"That [winning for him] was in my head for the last two weeks and I really wanted to do it for him. I know he's in hospital in his hospital bed, and he would have been watching this morning. It was nice to be able to get it done for him."

Race to Dubai success caps another strong campaign for McIlroy, who defended his Masters title in April to match Sir Nick Faldo's major tally, with the 37-year-old also proud to match Montgomerie's Order of Merit record.

"Winning eight Order of Merits was never really in my list of goals when I was growing up," the Northern Irishman said in an interview with the DP World Tour.

"I remember Monty being obviously a stalwart of the European Tour, going to watch him at the World Match Play at Wentworth over the years and remember playing with him for the first time, so to pull up alongside him and to win any of these things, it means the world to me.

"I am a very proud European, a proud European player. I am proud to be a part of the DP World Tour, and I am very proud of myself right now."

'Everything fell my way' - McIlroy reflects on Race to Dubai success

McIlroy threatened a late run for a fourth DP World Tour Championship title when he moved within a shot of the lead during the final day, having finished his front nine with three birdies in four holes, before eventually carding a bogey-free 67.

The birdie at the par-four 16th was enough to edge him top of the rankings ahead of Chacarra, who ended tied-third on eight under, with McIlroy briefly 0.1 points behind the Spaniard in the standings during the final day.

"It is probably a good thing but I wasn't aware of how much it was sort of going back and forth until the 16th," McIlroy added. "When I was walking to the green, I saw that he was projected No 1.

"Then when I made my birdie and I'm walking off the green, I saw I was projected No 1. I was a little nervous going to the last couple of holes. I guess I did what I needed to do and I shot a good score today.

"A lot of other things went my way today, as well. No one made a run. Eugenio [Chacarra] played pretty good, but none of the chasing pack did anything. There were a lot of different scenarios, but thankfully everything fell my way today."

Chacarra, who ends the season in second spot and has earned one of the 10 PGA Tour memberships available via the Race to Dubai rankings, said: "It was a good fight. I just came out short - that's the beauty of golf. He [McIlroy] has played here 14, 15 times, it was going to be tough, and he had a better day than I did.

"I knew it was going to be a long day and I tried my best. That's all I can ask for myself to do and that's what we did. I would say proud of the fight and proud to have a chance till the end."

articles.title: Tyrrell Hatton targets Ryder Cup return for Team Europe and major breakthrough after DP World Tour Championship win
articles.summary: Tyrrell Hatton finished five strokes clear of Rory McIlroy at the DP World Tour Championship, his ninth DP World Tour title; Hatton also finished runner-up last week in Abu Dhabi and ends the season third in the Race to Dubai standings
articles.body:
Hatton pulled clear of the field on the final day at Jumeirah Golf Estates, firing a six-under 66 to go one better than last week's runner-up finish at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship and claim a ninth DP World Tour title .

The win sees him end the DP World Tour season third in the Race to Dubai rankings, behind Rory McIlroy and Eugenio Chacarra, having entered the two season-ending play-offs outside of the top 50 after predominantly playing on LIV Golf this year.

Hatton's victory also lifts him to second in the European Ryder Cup rankings, ahead of next year's centenary contest at Adare Manor, with the Englishman determined to be part of Luke Donald's side once again in Ireland.

"It's an important time to try and earn Ryder Cup points," Hatton said after victory. "This [winning] helps a lot. I want to be on that team in a year's time. The last two weeks have been great, so I'm really proud of that."

On the prospect of playing alongside Race to Dubai winner McIlroy in next year's Ryder Cup team, he added in his press conference: "Rors [McIlroy] has had a pretty special career.

"He's going to go down as the best European golfer in history by the end of his career. I mean, he's first European to win the Grand Slam. He's now tied Monty [Colin Montgomerie] winning eight Race to Dubai titles.

"He's an unbelievable professional, and someone that you want around in the team room at the Ryder Cup. It's cool that I've been able to share four Ryder Cup teams with him and hopefully be able to make it five in Adare [Manor]."

Hatton posted top-seven finishes in two of the four majors this season, sharing third as McIlroy won The Masters before ended tied-seventh at the US Open, a record he is keen to build on next year alongside playing on the DP World Tour.

"In the last few years, my performances in majors have definitely got better," Hatton said. "Why that is, I don't know. I've not tried any differently - golf is just a weird game like that.

"I'd love to give myself a chance to win one. Like everyone out here playing in those tournaments, you dream of winning majors. Since I was a little boy, that's something I've wanted to do.

"I would love that to happen, and I'll work hard towards trying it make that happen. Time will tell if it works out."

McIlroy: Great to have Rahm and Hatton back!

Hatton's victory is a fourth in six DP World Tour events for a former LIV Golf players, following on from Adrian Meronk at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, Chacarra at the DP World Tour India Championship and Rahm in Abu Dhabi.

"For the Ryder Cup team and points, you want guys like Tyrrell [Hatton] and Jon [Rahm] and that calibre of player to make the team automatically, so that Luke wouldn't have to waste a pick on them, essentially," McIlroy explained.

"I always see these things through the lens of the Ryder Cup and it's great that they are back on the DP World Tour. It's great that they don't have the noise that they were dealing with over the past few months. They can just focus on their games and get back to what they love doing."

On how impressive Hatton's victory was former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley told Sky Sports : "He has been playing a lot here in Europe in the last few years and we've seen this kind of quality from him. This time he happened to get over the line, after a couple of second-place finishes here before.

"He's a fantastic golfer, and that's the bottom line. It's easy to focus on his histrionics on the golf course, his body language and the moaning and groaning that goes on, but take that aside and just watch the quality of play that he has.

"You look at his chipping, putting, iron-play and driving, you look at all of those things, then you factor in that he's got a great heart and a real understanding of how to play this game - he is the real full package."

The new DP World Tour season begins at the BMW Australian PGA Championship from November 26-29, held at The Lakes GC in Sydney.
