articles.title: Trump Blasts Judge's 2-Week Halt to His Washington Golf Project and Says Administration Will Appeal
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump on Sunday decried a "highly destructive and political decision" from a federal judge after she ordered a two-week delay on renovations at a historic Washington public golf course that he has been trying to redevelop into a championship-level venue.
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump on Sunday decried a "highly destructive and political decision" from a federal judge after she ordered a two-week delay on renovations at a historic Washington public golf course that he has been trying to redevelop into a championship-level venue.

In a social media post, Trump said his administration will "immediately appeal, on an expedited basis" the temporary restraining order from U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes, which she issued just before East Potomac Golf Links was due to close Sunday for 15 months.

"It is in a terrible state of disrepair, as anybody can see by just looking at the pictures that are now circulating all over the Country, and in the Court," said Trump, who spent much of the weekend posting photos on his social media site of the golf course. "They don't call it Trash Island for no reason!"

Trump had announced work on the site along the Potomac River would begin that day despite the legal challenge initiated against the project in February by the DC Preservation League and two local golfers.

The plaintiffs argue that the president's plan would change the character of the accessible golf course and make it unaffordable, something Trump has denied. They had sought the stop-work order, saying that closing the course and launching work on the project would "irreparably injure plaintiffs and the public interest."

The president's public announcements on social media last month outlining the date of the closure of East Potomac Park and linking it to the renovation of the golf course weighed heavily in the judge's decision.

Reyes, in her ruling Saturday, noted that those posts presented a problem for the government, indicating that Trump's redevelopment plan was final and that the National Park Service "will close the Park to implement it."

Both points, she wrote, "favor granting Plaintiffs' motion for another temporary restraining order."

The order is in effect through Nov. 28. The park's redevelopment is one of multiple projects in the nation's capital that Trump has championed to remake the city. They include a large memorial arch, a White House ballroom and the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, among others.

Reyes' order was the latest in a series of rulings in lawsuits challenging Trump's projects that were issued just hours before construction was expected to begin. A different judge recently ordered a 14-day delay on work for the arch, a decision that came shortly after a key planning commission stacked with Trump appointees approved plans for the project.

articles.title: DP World Tour chief executive explains why including ex-LIV Golf members in 2027 is 'huge opportunity' to strengthen events
articles.summary: The deadline to confirm DP World Tour membership for 2027 ended on Sunday; Guy Kinnings discussed on Sky Sports Golf how they plan to welcome LIV Golfers onto their circuit next season, with more details to be announced in the coming days
articles.body:
The deadline to confirm DP World Tour membership for the 2027 season ended on Sunday following the conclusion of the Race to Dubai campaign, with multiple LIV Golfers set to be more frequently involved over the coming year.

The decision to include some past LIV players has caused debate from current DP World Tour members, although Kinnings believes it can enhance tournaments during times when the golfing calendar is focused on the PGA Tour.

"We're going to assess [membership applications] and then we'll make an announcement on Tuesday about that," Kinnings exclusively told Sky Sports .

"For us, it's the prospect of having incredible talent joining our tour, which already is laden with talent.

"There's the top 100 that have kept their DP World Tour cards, 15 coming from HotelPlanner Tour, 20 from Tour School. Top players coming from all of our global partnerships - all of that together will lead to significantly stronger fields.

"What it does is it brings it [strength in fields] at the time of year when our dual members are off in the United States and that will help those [DP World Tour] tournaments at that time of year.

"That will make happy promoters, happy sponsors, happy broadcasters, hopefully happy fans. We see it as a huge opportunity and what it will be is at the right time and hopefully great strong fields throughout the year."

Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton are expected to play full-time on the DP World Tour in 2027, with golfers ineligible for 12 months on the PGA Tour from their previous LIV Golf start, while Bryson DeChambeau is yet to confirm whether he will accept membership as a recent major champion.

Golf Channel LA reported that Niemann would play "approximately 15 DP World Tour tournaments through wild cards, a number that could increase if he wins a title", having previous won nine times on LIV Golf.

Ex-LIV golfers Thomas Pieters, Michael La Sasso and Carlos Ortiz all have invites to the BMW Australian PGA Championship, the opening event of the new season, with deals reportedly expected to be agreed on how many DP World Tour starts players will get.

The PGA Tour is undergoing significant changes to its schedule from 2028, with a Championship Series and Challenger Series running concurrently, while discussions are ongoing to finalise the pathway - and how many cards - that will be available from the DP World Tour to the US-based tour.

"I think with the PGA Tour clearly planning from 2028 onwards to focus their tour in that February to August time, it gives us a chance to build and strengthen what we have in that time around the world," Kinnings added.

"It also give us the opportunity from the start of September to the end of January to really have the very strongest tournaments around the world. We can shine a light on international golf with some stunning fields.

"So, working together with them [PGA Tour], I think there's a huge opportunity for us both. We're in the middle of very positive conversations (with the PGA Tour). We're hoping to have news certainly by the New Year."

McIlroy: Ex-LIV Golfers will make Race to Dubai 'even more difficult'

Rory McIlroy said earlier this month he hopes the men's professional game can now stabilise after a turbulent few years, with the world No 2 expecting ex-LIV Golf members to make his hopes of winning a record ninth Race to Dubai title in 2027 a tougher challenge.

"Next year [winning the Race to Dubai] is going to be tough because you've got the likes of Jon [Rahm] and Tyrrell [Hatton] and some of these guys coming back [from LIV Golf] and playing a full-time DP World Tour schedule," McIlroy explained in his press conference.

"Obviously I'll be sort of bouncing around a little bit on both the DP World Tour and the PGA Tour, so I think The Race to Dubai next year is going to be incredibly competitive.

"I reckon it's going to be a little more difficult [to win]. Not that it's not difficult every year, but even more difficult next year with those guys playing a full-time schedule over here. I'll just have to go out there and play well and accumulate points early.

"If I have to maybe Beef up my schedule at the end of next year to try to compete with them, if I'm in with a close enough chance of doing it, I'll do that."

articles.title: He’s 19, just won $1 million and made PGA Tour history. But Blades Brown hasn’t forgotten what matters most
articles.summary: Blades Brown is living the dream right now.
articles.body: Blades Brown is living the dream right now. At 19 years, five months and 25 days old, the teenage American just enjoyed the sweetest moment of his fledgling career: becoming the PGA Tour’s youngest winner since 1931. It was a life-changing, breakthrough win at the World Wide Technology Championship, emotionally shared with the only Brown family member present that day in Los Cabos: His beloved father, Parke, who was fighting back tears amid his son’s dramatic playoff victory. “It was so special being able to give him a big old bear hug after we’d won the golf tournament. He was trying to take a picture, but his hands were shaking because he was so nervous,” Blades Brown told CNN Sports. It was a moment made all the sweeter by what the Brown family has been through. Four years ago, Parke Brown was diagnosed with bone cancer and given just months to live, though doctors later found out he actually had a rare form of leukemia that, thankfully, can be treated. His father’s fight with cancer has taught Blades a lot of hard lessons very early in life. “Unfortunately, with leukemia, it never really goes away. Luckily, he has a leukemia that is extremely treatable. But one thing that he has taught me is to be a warrior. I remember I went and visited him a couple of times in the hospital, and he looked at me and said, ‘Blades, I love my family,’” Blades Brown said. “It puts a whole new perspective on life whenever a loved one has death looking him right back in the face. I’ve learned so much from my dad and I’ve still got a lot to learn and especially with the next chapter of my life being here on the PGA Tour,” the teenager added. Sporting excellence is something that’s par for the course for the Browns – to such an extent that Blades considers himself only the third best athlete in the family. It was Parke who first introduced his son to golf. Blades’ older sister Millie has just finished up her collegiate career as a basketball standout, while his mother, Rhonda, is a trailblazer in her own right, sinking the very first three-point basket in WNBA history while playing for the New York Liberty in 1997. “She’s my mom. She does a phenomenal job. Every single time that I finish a golf tournament, she’s always the first one to text me. She’s helped so much with my professional life so far. Having somebody else in the family that’s been a professional athlete that kind of knows the world, it really is such a blessing and we’re enjoying every second of it,” Blades Brown said. The teenager – who concedes he’s probably too short for a career in basketball – is now fully focused on all things golf. Blades Brown turned professional in late 2024 when he was just 17, having decided to skip college golf altogether. The young American is well aware of the sacrifices his parents made for him along the way, something for which he remains forever grateful. “You only have two parents, or two real parents, that is, and I’m really close to my mom and dad, and they’ve just poured so much time and effort and love into me,” Blades said. Blades Brown has been dreaming big from a very young age and, when it comes to making history, he got started on that at a pretty early age too. Brown was just 16 when he became the youngest ever US Amateur stroke-play medalist, breaking the iconic Bobby Jones’ 103-year-old record in the process. The Tennessee teenager, who’s also competing this weekend in Austin, Texas, has now also secured a full PGA Tour card after his momentous triumph in Mexico. With that come many perks, including future tournament exemptions and the chance to play in next year’s PGA Championship, one of golf’s four major tournaments. Oh, and there’s also the very nice paycheck of just over one million dollars. In fact, given Brown’s current momentum, a place on America’s Ryder Cup team next year in Ireland might even be on the cards. Though the pressure of that tournament is immense, Blades Brown plays fearless golf and that’s no real surprise for someone who earned a black belt in taekwondo when he was younger. When it comes to sporting idols, though, just like so many other youngsters from all over the world, Blades Brown credits the great Tiger Woods as having a major impact on his life. “I’ve probably seen every single YouTube video there is of Tiger Woods. I love watching his game. I want to try to replicate everything that he can do on the golf course because what he was able to do with the golf ball was so special. I remember his 2000 season, what he’s been able to accomplish with four majors in a row, that’s unheard of,” the Nashville native reflected. “I actually had the pleasure of meeting him at the 2024 US Junior Amateur when his son Charlie Woods was playing in the event. And I just remember thinking, this guy’s hands feel like two 14-ounce ribeyes. These things have hit so many golf balls. I was on cloud nine when I was talking to him. “I can’t remember anything he said to me or anything that I said to him, but it was really special getting to meet him.”

articles.title: Emotional Rory McIlroy dedicates record 8th Race to Dubai title to father Gerry
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy tied a record with his eighth Race to Dubai title, dedicating the emotional win to his recovering father.
articles.body:
Rory McIlroy put together a historic Sunday at Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai, but his emotion after a record-tying Race to Dubai title had nothing to do with the latest trophy going into his cabinet at home.

McIlroy, the world No. 2, finished at 10 under in the DP World Tour Championship, placing solo second behind Tyrrell Hatton but, more importantly, two shots in front of Eugenio Chacarra. That gave him enough points to win another Race to Dubai title, the DP World Tour's season-long points race. It's his eighth time to claim the honor, tying Colin Montgomerie for the most in the history of the DP World Tour.

After the round, McIlroy was overcome with emotion. He revealed his father, Gerry, has been hospitalized for the past two months after a double lung transplant in September. He spent numerous days in ICU, but the procedure was a success, and Gerry is recovering well, McIlroy said. That doesn't mean his family hasn't gone through some challenging moments the past few weeks.

"My dad -- hopefully everyone's dad in this room -- is a massive part of my life, and has been my biggest supporter, is the one that got me into the game and the one that told me to follow my dreams and never give up and never think that you're not good enough or you're not big enough," McIlroy said. "He's been making a really steady recovery. I went up to see him before I left for Abu Dhabi a couple of weeks ago, and he said to me, 'Rors, go and win me The Race to Dubai.'

"So that was, you know -- that was in my head for the last two weeks, and I really wanted to do it for him and I know he's in hospital in his hospital bed, and he would have been watching this morning. It was nice to be able to get it done for him."

Chacarra, the young Spaniard who earned a PGA Tour card on Sunday thanks to his finish in the Race to Dubai, led in the standings with one event to go, but McIlroy finished one spot ahead on the leaderboard, giving him enough points to claim victory to the season-long prize.

McIlroy was sure to compliment his European ally after the conclusion of play Sunday, saying Chacarra looks like a player who will be an asset for the Euro side in coming Ryder Cups. Chacarra, if his play that earned him a PGA Tour card continues, is a strong candidate to make the team at Adare Manor come next September.

In 2026, McIlroy has only one worldwide win, defending his title at the Masters. He marveled at his consistency after the round, saying he's proud of constantly putting himself in contention, even if he didn't win as many trophies as he would've liked.

"But if you're going to win one, the Masters is not a bad one to do," he joked.

More importantly was tying Monty's record. McIlroy has long spoken about his goal to join the Scot on top of the DP World Tour record books as one of the most successful players in the Tour's history.

Sunday's result makes it even more solid what was already well known: McIlroy may just be the best European golfer of all time.

"They don't get any less special, I'll tell you that," McIlroy said. "And this one, I had to work hard for this one this week. Eugenio has obviously had a great week himself, and yeah, I think the last couple were maybe a little less stressful than this one.

"Very proud to win this again, and yeah, put my name alongside Monty's with eight, and we'll go again next year and try to get one more."

Cameron Jourdan is an assistant editor of Golfweek, covering college and amateur golf, the PGA Tour and plenty more. Follow Cameron on X/Twitter (@Cam_Jourdan) or Instagram (@GolfweekJourdan).

articles.title: The Annika: Lindy Duncan wins her first LPGA Tour title after 222 starts
articles.summary: It took 222 starts and more than 10 years on the tour to get it, but Lindy Duncan secured her first LPGA victory when she won The Annika on Sunday; She pulled away from Hye-Jin Choi, finishing two strokes ahead as she shot a 67 in round four to finish at 16 under par
articles.body:
She'd never even had a share of an LPGA lead LPGA until Friday at Pelican Golf Club but two key birdies saw her pull away from Hye-Jin Choi and finish two strokes ahead as she shot a 67 in round four to close at 16 under par.

It took her 222 starts and more than 10 years on the tour to get this win.

"To be here, I'm just completely shocked," Duncan said afterwards. "I just put so much pressure on myself because I really want to do well and the competition is so great out here.

"Sometimes you just over-try and I think I've done that a lot. This week I just finally let that go a little bit.

"Just keep going. You never know when it's going to turn around for you. Momentum is such a strange thing. You keep working on the right things and anything's possible."

Duncan tapped in a four-foot par putt on the final hole, and a long line of LPGA players waited to douse water on her to share in her celebration.

Duncan, 35, is the oldest first-time winner on the LPGA since Leta Lindley who was 36 when she won the Corning Classic in 2008.

On Sunday she had fallen two shots behind when Choi birdied the 11th.

But Choi had a three-putt bogey from 50 feet at the front of the green on the 13th, and two holes later the South Korean had to scramble for bogey to fall into a tie.

Duncan took over from there with two shots she won't soon forget. Her approach to the 16th was well right of the pin and went up the back slope, narrowly missing a sprinkler head and rolling back down a slope to six feet for birdie and a one-shot lead.

She drove into a bunker on the 17th and faced a shot to a pin just beyond a deep bunker. It came out beautifully to 20 feet and Duncan holed that birdie and took a two-shot lead.

Choi had to settle for her third runner-up finish in her last three tournaments. Choi has gone 127 starts on the LPGA without winning.

Haeran Ryu and Yuri Yoshida tied for third. Julia Lopez Ramirez finished fifth.

Nelly Korda, playing for the first time in two months, closed with a 67 and finished seventh, six shots behind. Korda needs one more win to qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame, her next chance coming in the season finale in Naples.

England's Lottie Woad finished tied in ninth place at eight under par.

articles.title: ‘So Happy for Him,’ ‘He’s What We Needed’ — NFL Fans React to Kirk Cousins Getting Emotional After Leading Minnesota to Huge Win vs. Packers

articles.body:
Kirk Cousins had plenty of reasons to enjoy beating Green Bay, but getting through the postgame interview proved a little harder.

Back in a Vikings uniform at the stadium where his first stint with Minnesota ended, Cousins became emotional discussing the road that brought him back. Fans who watched the moment were ready to welcome him home, even if this particular reunion happened on enemy territory.

Kirk Cousins' Return Hits Home With Vikings Fans

Minnesota defeated the Packers 30-10 at Lambeau Field on Sunday, with Cousins completing 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception. The victory pushed the Vikings to 7-2 and completed a season sweep of their division rival.

The significance went well beyond another win in the standings.

Cousins suffered his season-ending Achilles injury at Lambeau in October 2023, during what became the final game of his first Minnesota tenure. Returning there in purple and gold brought those memories back.

"I tore my Achilles here and it's been a tough three years," Cousins said in an emotional interview shared by ESPN's Lindsey Thiry .

One fan immediately connected the two afternoons.

"So happy for him to get a win at Lambeau, where his last game as a Viking happened when he tore his Achilles. Welcome home!" the fan wrote .

Another supporter had already seen enough to endorse the reunion.

"SKOL!!💛🏈💜So great to see him back, he's what we needed!!!" the fan wrote .

There is a pretty good recipe for winning over Minnesota fans. Put on the purple, beat the Packers, and give everyone a reason to feel something afterward. Cousins checked every box on Sunday.

Cousins Gives Minnesota an Encouraging First Chapter

The Vikings reacquired Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 third-round pick at the trade deadline. That left him only a handful of days to prepare for his first start back with the organization.

He now ranks ninth with a PFN QB Impact Score of 80.7 across his 10 appearances this season. Sunday provided an encouraging opening to the Minnesota portion of that campaign.

The affection in the replies was just as obvious.

"Kirko forever on lovewatch man🥹," one fan wrote .

"So proud of you," another supporter wrote .

One fan shared the interview with a three-word declaration.

Cousins also had considerable help. Minnesota's defense produced four turnovers and eight sacks, while Justin Jefferson caught nine passes for 74 yards. When Green Bay threatened to make things interesting, Cousins finished a long touchdown drive with a 20-yard scoring pass to Gavin Bartholomew.

That gave the afternoon substance beyond the reunion itself. Minnesota needed production from its returning quarterback, and Cousins delivered enough to let a dominant defensive performance turn into a comfortable victory.

One game will not answer every question about where this partnership goes. It did give Cousins a much happier memory of a stadium that had carried a painful one for three years.

For the fans welcoming him back, a win over Green Bay was a particularly thoughtful housewarming gift.

articles.title: Austin Championship: Trace Crowe grabs 54-hole lead late
articles.summary: The third round of the Austin Championship was played in groupings off split tees after darkness cut the end of Round 2 short Friday. Here's what happened on...
articles.body:
Trace Crowe birdied his final two holes Saturday to get to 14 under and separate himself from three other players through 54 holes of the inaugural Austin Championship .

Chad Ramey, Erik van Rooyen and Sami Valimaki all could have shared the lead heading into Sunday's final round at Fazio Canyons Golf Course if Crowe had faltered down the stretch.

But the 30-year-old Crowe, who is seeking his first win on Tour this week in Texas, birdied the par-3 17th and followed it up with another circle at No. 18 as part of the final grouping on the course.

"It was like 220 straight into the wind, I was just trying to hit a 4-iron as low as I could and push it just a touch," Crowe recalled. "It was actually a pretty good shot to end up in that bunker, it was a good leave.

He called the lie perfect as it was just sitting uphill.

"It just came out perfect and went in — me and my caddie both had a feeling I was going to make that before we got it, so it was pretty cool to see that go in," he added.

Heavy winds began to impact players still on their back nines Saturday afternoon, and Crowe was no exception.

After setting the course record on Thursday with an opening-round 62, Crowe bogeyed the first two holes on his back nine on Moving Day.

Another square at the par-4 16th put his chances in doubt but the run of birdies at the end of his round vaulted him ahead for the solo lead.

Americans Ben Kohles and Max Greyserman are two back of Crowe's lead, while eight players sit T-7 at 11 under.

Ramey had the clubhouse lead for more than an hour. He got there by limiting mistakes — the 34-year-old Mississippi State alum has posted just three bogeys, one in each round. Saturday's error came at the par-3 17th, the same hole Crowe birdied from an hour later.

"On a week like this to kind of finally get some good results and be in a good position going into Sunday, it's great to see," said Ramey, who entered the week No. 136 in the FedExCup Fall standings and has moved up to a projected No. 68.

The Austin Championship tees off at Omni Barton Creek Resort & Spa in Austin, Texas.

That would give Ramey a card for 2027, despite not having a top 10 finish in his first 26 starts.

Valimaki, who won for the first time at the RSM Classic last November , moved into the co-leader position with a 3-under 69. He opened the inaugural tournament 68-66 after making his first PGA Tour start since July at last week's WWT Championship.

"It was good to take some time off, it's actually been a long time since I felt like I could enjoy the golf course and I feel like that's the biggest key for me," said Valimaki, who battled a right wrist injury and also received stiches in his left hand.

The Finnish player was No. 172 entering the week but has crept up to No. 129 with 18 holes left.

The top 100 players earn their cards , while players inside the top 125 earn conditional status for the 2027 season.

Van Rooyen was more up and down with his 69 on Saturday. He bogeyed the 215-yard, par-3 eighth hole and followed that up with a double at the turn. A bogey at the 17th looked like it could sink his chances at the co-lead, but he answered by circling the par-5 18th.

"Compared to the first two days, it's much trickier," said the South African, who has moved from No. 140 in the fall standings up to No. 108 with his play in Austin. "Wind was difficult. I thought some of the pins were really tricky, and it was cold so the ball's just not going as far."

Crowe, who would become the 11th first-time winner of the 2026 Tour season , called the pressure of closing out "another golf tournament" but also noted the weather would be a challenge.

"Keeping your head down, being patient and just seeing where it puts us at the end," he said. "Just got to drive it on the fairway and have to make a few putts."

The final round has been moved up due to inclement weather expected in the area on Sunday. Groups of three will go off on split tees between 8 and 10 a.m.

Golf Channel's TV coverage starts at 12:30 p.m. ET.

The Austin Championship will go an extra day. Inclement weather wiped out Sunday's play, leading the PGA Tour to move the full final round to Monday.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins emotional after Vikings win: 'It's been a tough three years'
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins led the Vikings to a win in his first start with the team since 2023. He was emotional after enduring a "tough three years."
articles.body:
Kirk Cousins led the Minnesota Vikings to a 30-10 win over the Green Bay Packers in his first start back with the team since being reacquired in a pre-trade deadline deal with the Las Vegas Raiders .

The 38-year-old signal-caller was nearly moved to tears reflecting on the win, which came at Lambeau Field, the very venue his initial stint with the Vikings ended.

"It was emotional coming to the stadium. Three years ago, tearing my Achilles here," Cousins said with his voice breaking in a postgame interview with ESPN's Lindsey Thiry . "It's been a tough three years. I was just grateful for the opportunity to play here today. Grateful for my teammates and what they did today to make this outcome possible."

Cousins spent six years with the Vikings after signing with the team as a free agent in 2018. The end of his initial stint in Minnesota came in 2023, when he was enjoying one of the best seasons of his career, earning early-season MVP buzz while posting a 103.8 passer rating in a contract year.

However, Cousins' final season in Minnesota ended prematurely. He tore his Achilles in the Vikings' Week 8 game against the Packers, ending his season and sending him into free agency, where he landed with the Atlanta Falcons.

NFL Week 10 reactions after wins, big moments and breakout performances

Cousins struggled to find his footing with the Falcons, splitting time as a starter with Michael Penix Jr. before landing with the Raiders to start the 2026 season. The pre-deadline trade brought him back to Minnesota, and the veteran seemed relieved to be given an opportunity to enjoy a full-circle moment after his trying, post-Vikings stint.

"It's been a tough three years," he reiterated. "There's more to the story being written."

Included in that story will be star receiver Justin Jefferson , with whom Cousins acknowledged he was particularly happy to reunite.

"I love being back with him," Cousins said when asked about Jefferson. "He's a competitor. He's a lot of fun to play with."

Jefferson logged nine catches for 74 yards in Cousins' 2026 Vikings debut, marking a season-high in receptions.

But while Cousins is excited about that connection and the Vikings' offense in general, he knows that the team's path to contention will be driven by the performance of Brian Flores' elite stop unit.

"We can talk about offense, but it's the defense," Cousins said. "The defense won us the football game today. They're always gonna give us a chance."

articles.title: LPGA Tour: Lindy Duncan wins The Annika for first title after 222 events
articles.summary: American Lindy Duncan wins The Annika for her first LPGA Tour title after playing in 222 events over 12 years.
articles.body:
16 L Duncan (US); -14 HJ Choi (Kor); -13 Y Yoshida (Jap), H Ryu (Kor); -12 J Lopez Ramirez (Spa); - 11 G Lopez (Mex); - 10 N Korda (US)

Selected others: -8 L Woad (Eng); -4 L Maguire (Ire), C Hull (Eng); +9 J Ewart Shadoff (Eng); +17 M Rhodes (Eng)

American Lindy Duncan was left "completely shocked" after winning her first LPGA Tour title at the 222nd time of asking.

The 35-year-old started Sunday's final round of The Annika with a one-shot lead and two late birdies saw her claim victory.

Duncan, who joined the tour in 2014, had only enjoyed one top-10 finish this season.

But her three-under-par 67 saw her finish on 16 under at Pelican Golf Club in Belleair, Florida, two shots clear of her nearest challenger, South Korea's Choi Hye-jin .

"I got so many people to thank that believed in me when I wasn't sure if I wanted to keep playing or if I was good enough to keep playing," Duncan said followng her win.

"To be here, I'm just completely shocked."

Duncan was tied for the lead with Choi with two holes left to play before her late heroics.

"Coming into today I kind of thought, 'No matter what happens I learned a huge lesson,' and hopefully I can take that forward with me," Duncan said.

"I just put so much pressure on myself because I really want to do well. Sometimes you just over try, and I think I've done that a lot. This week I finally let that go a little bit."

The win also saw her qualify as one of the 60 players at the season-ending CME Group Tour Championship by jumping from 74 to 34 in the standings for the season-long points race.

World number one Nelly Korda, who finished seventh, will be aiming to win her second season title next week.

England's Lottie Woad - another player in the field for next week's finale - was two shots further back but it was enough to secure a top-10 spot.

articles.title: Rams’ Aaron Donald opens up on health status after win vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: Aaron Donald gave the Los Angeles Rams another reason to feel good after their 42-10 win over the Arizona Cardinals. The veteran defensive tackle recorded 1....
articles.body:
Aaron Donald gave the Los Angeles Rams another reason to feel good after their 42-10 win over the Arizona Cardinals. The veteran defensive tackle recorded 1.5 sacks that ended a lengthy drought and cleared out any doubts regarding his physical condition heading into the team's bye week.

Donald described his true emotions after the victory, particularly because the Rams' defense spent relatively little time on the field. However, he still wants to use the break to get fully healthy before the team's final stretch.

"Get back right, get myself feeling 100% and get ready for this run," Donald said.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The performance against Arizona marked Donald's first sack in 1,050 days. That stretch included two seasons in retirement before he returned to the Rams in late August. His previous sack came on New Year's Eve in 2023 against the New York Giants.

Donald finished Sunday's game with an eight-game streak without one. He also moved past Justin Houston and Chandler Jones, who each finished their careers with 112 sacks, into 31st place on the NFL's all-time list.

The Rams' defense delivered an impressive performance apart from just Donald's individual numbers. Los Angeles held Arizona to 123 total yards and six first downs, both the lowest totals by any team this season. The Cardinals also failed to convert any of their six third-down attempts.

Additionally, head coach Sean McVay praised Donald's continued impact on the team.

"I'm never surprised," McVay said. "He never ceases to amaze me. I think the term '1 of 1' is thrown around way too loosely this day and age, but it's not with him. He's 1 of 1."

The Rams have won four straight games after opening the season 2-4. They will use their Week 11 bye to recover before returning to action against the Green Bay Packers.

articles.title: Examining 4 Bucks Players Who Could Attract Trade Interest Right Now
articles.summary: As the Bucks continue to spiral out of control, we explore four players who have the most trade value at the moment.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Bucks have had a less than favorable start to the 2026-27 season. Although a weaker record was expected in light of Giannis Antetokounmpo 's departure in the offseason, a 1-13 record following their latest 113-106 loss to the Atlanta Hawks was probably not part of the plan.

Needless to say, the Bucks find themselves in uncharted territory as they sit at the bottom of the Eastern Conference. Despite having some talented pieces on their roster, most of whom have the potential to be assets in the future, Milwaukee finds itself in a position where it must make upgrades soon.

In this regard, there have been rumblings suggesting that the Bucks could be sellers in the trade market once the activity begins to rise.

For the most part, players such as Brayden Burries and Nate Ament may not be on the trade block, primarily because of their rookie status. Meanwhile, veterans like Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner , both of whom have been mentioned in trade rumors , may not have many takers.

Thus, while gauging Milwaukee's roster, it is apparent that there are only a handful of players who have real trade value. On that note, we examine the four players who can draw the most interest right now.

One of the Bucks' most valuable trade assets at this point is Jaime Jaquez Jr. After acquiring the guard in the trade that sent Antetokounmpo to the Heat, there were expectations that he could become a solid rotation piece for Milwaukee. While he has been remarkable as an individual, the team's poor performance could see him placed on the trade block.

Jaquez has essentially positioned himself as a Swiss Army knife on offense. As a capable multi-level scorer, the guard can consistently create scoring opportunities for himself. Having improved as a perimeter threat, the 27-year-old has only expanded his offensive repertoire.

This season has arguably been Jaquez's best one. Having earned a larger offensive role, Jaquez posted 16.5 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 2.8 assists per game while shooting 48.1% from the field and 44.1% from three-point range before Sunday night's game.

As impressive as this is, when considering that he is in the final year of his contract and has a cap hit of just $5.9 million, the 25-year-old has the potential to be a phenomenal low-cost pickup. Hence, even though the Bucks may not get much back for him in terms of player assets, the draft compensation could be worthwhile.

Like Jaquez, another Bucks guard who will likely generate considerable trade interest in the coming weeks is AJ Green.

Green has established himself as a lethal sharpshooter with impressive off-ball movement and relocation on offense. For all intents and purposes, when it comes to perimeter shooting, the 27-year-old is incredibly effective.

This season, the guard is averaging 6.0 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 1.4 assists per game while shooting 42.6% from three-point range. Given that he plays roughly 17.3 minutes a night and attempts 4.2 three-pointers per game, these splits are quite impressive.

Like most players on this list, Green has also experienced a drastic reduction in playing time this season, which is likely a product of Milwaukee's plans to develop the young talent on the team. Needless to say, this could be indicative of the 27-year-old's availability on the trade block. On a promising note, however, Milwaukee can expect good returns for him.

AJ Green is currently in the first year of a four-year, $45 million contract. Given his cap hit of $10.0 million this season, the Bucks could realistically acquire expiring contracts or young players. Regardless, given his value as a player, Milwaukee stands to benefit from trading him.

The next player on this list who is likely to attract attention in the trade market is Kel'el Ware .

Like Jaquez, Ware also joined the Bucks as part of the deal sending Antetokounmpo to the Heat. Given the environment in Miami, there is reason to believe that joining Milwaukee would help the big man's talent flourish. To that extent, his performances during the preseason also seemed promising . Unfortunately, his display in the regular season has been rather bland thus far.

In 13 appearances for Milwaukee before Sunday's game, Kel'el Ware was averaging 8.6 points, 6.5 rebounds, 0.5 steals, and 1.1 blocks per game on 40.8% shooting from the field.

Surprisingly, these seem like solid stats considering that he only averaged 17.7 minutes per game, often coming off the bench. However, given his potential, it may be worth asking why a player like him is playing fewer minutes in the first place.

In light of his performances, there may not be many teams willing to take on his $4.6 million contract in a direct trade. However, if the Bucks manage to package Ware with another player asset, the 22-year-old could be perceived as a valuable add-on.

Aside from Ament, it doesn't seem like any of the Bucks' big men are left off the trade block. While Myles Turner and Kel'el Ware have been mentioned in trade rumors before, Bucks backup center Jericho Sims has also drawn some attention lately.

Sims doesn't possess the tools to be an elite starting quality big man. However, with his athleticism, rebounding, and sheer shot-blocking potential, the 28-year-old positions himself as a consistent lob threat and a viable rim protector.

Despite his potential, Sims has seen a distinct dip in his playing time this season, resulting in reduced averages of 0.5 points, 1.1 rebounds, and 0.1 blocks per game. Still, when noting his career averages of 3.0 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 0.4 blocks per game on 73.8% shooting from the field, especially on an expiring contract worth $2.8 million, he could become a solid end-of-bench center.

Much like Ware, Sims may not have much value on his own. However, if the Bucks opt not to take back salary for him and only prioritize draft compensation, there may be some interested buyers.

articles.title: Norfolk council considers 'unfair burden' of major energy schemes
articles.summary: It comes as nearly 50,000 people sign a petition opposing plans for a £25bn solar farm.
articles.body:
Nearly 50,000 people have signed a petition opposing plans for a huge data centre and solar farm in the countryside, as critics warn the region could be unfairly burdened by energy projects.

The Borough Council of King's Lynn and West Norfolk is considering what it can do to oppose a number of major schemes, which include the Longmarsh Green Energy Project.

The developer Evolution Power Limited (EPL) wants to build a 1.3GW solar farm alongside a data centre, which would need up to 1 gigawatt of power at any one time, near King's Lynn.

The £25bn proposal coincides with other large solar farms proposed for the rural area. Decisions on the schemes will be made by central government departments.

An extraordinary meeting is being held on Monday evening to decide how the council responds to seven major infrastructure projects.

Councillors will be asked to oppose renewable energy developments that "lack meaningful local support, threaten productive farmland and wildlife, or fail to provide direct local benefit".

The report going before councillors, put forward by the Independent council leader Alistair Beales, also calls for Norfolk councils to join forces and lobby the energy secretary to ensure "our region is not unfairly burdened".

They will also vote on whether to challenge ministers' final decisions in the courts where that is "warranted in the interests of local residents".

Because of the size of the schemes, the final say on all of them rests with the government rather than the local council.

Of particular concern is the Longmarsh project, which would cover 4,695 acres (1,900 hectares) of farmland across two sites - one near Tilney St Lawrence and the other near Fincham and Barton Bendish.

North West Norfolk's Conservative MP James Wild has said the solar farm and data centre "could represent further large-scale industrialisation of the landscape".

EPL said the scheme would create thousands of construction jobs and was "critical for future UK economic growth".

The other projects in the area include The Droves solar farm near Swaffham, Redmere wind farm , the Wisbech incinerator project , National Grid energy upgrades in Walpole and the Fens Reservoir .

The meeting will take place at 17:00 GMT at King's Lynn Minster and it will also be livestreamed via the council's YouTube channel.
